claims.text: Introducing an open-porosity 3D lattice into HfMoTaTiZr will reduce bulk density while largely maintaining room- and high-temperature mechanical performance.
The baseline HfMoTaTiZr is an as-cast, fully dense material with a density of approximately 10.21 g/cm³.
HfMoTaTiZr has a room-temperature yield strength of approximately 1600 MPa.
The baseline HfMoTaTiZr has an elevated-temperature yield strength of approximately 855 MPa.
The proposed intervention is additive manufacturing of a periodic HfMoTaTiZr lattice with a 300–500 μm cell size.
The lattice will introduce uniformly distributed open porosity.
The open porosity will reduce the bulk density.
Continuous load-bearing struts will favor stress distribution through the lattice.
Replacing solid volume with controlled voids lowers overall mass.
Additive manufacture of the lattice will not alter the alloy's intrinsic microstructure.
Preservation of the intrinsic microstructure will maintain the alloy's inherent yield strength at room temperature and approximately 1000°C.
Optimized lattice geometry will minimize stress concentrations and enable high load transfer along the struts.
The lattice is predicted to reduce bulk density by approximately 15–20% relative to the fully dense baseline.
The lattice is predicted to cause only a minor, if any, reduction in compressive yield strength at room temperature and high temperature.
The alloy composition must remain unchanged by the intervention.
Mechanical evaluation is restricted to compressive loading at approximately 25°C and 1000°C.
Failure to obtain at least a 15% density reduction will falsify the hypothesis.
A compressive yield-strength loss greater than 10% at either room temperature or 1000°C will falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The proposal repeatedly describes the lattice specimens as being made from or remaining 'as-cast' HfMoTaTiZr while specifying additive manufacturing as the fabrication route. An additively manufactured specimen is not itself as-cast unless 'as-cast' refers only to feedstock provenance, which is not clarified.
